drains.note: Measured and estimated totals are separate and are never summed into a single "total pollution" figure. Only 2 of 97 drains have a published flow; 95 have no published flow or BOD at all. Telangana MPRs count 54 Godavari + 13 Maneru + 11 Nakkavagu/Manjeera + 5 Karakavagu/Kinnerasani drains but never name or locate them, so they are not in this file.

top_10_by_bod_tpd.drain: Nashik city nallas - aggregate uncollected sewage

stps.note: NGT compliance is derived from per-plant effluent values in the Maharashtra MPR Mar 2026 annexure where published (3 plants meet NGT norms: Shirdi 16 MLD, Chandrapur Pathanpura 45 MLD, Rehmat Nagar 25 MLD). No per-plant total nitrogen or faecal coliform value is published anywhere, and 123 of 149 plants have no effluent value at all, so "0 meeting NGT" would be a data limit, not a finding. All 12 Nagpur plants are Non-Comply. 80 plants are still proposed (510.5 MLD) and 18 under construction (714.25 MLD) — they are included so towns without a working plant do not vanish; operational_status therefore uses four values (operational / not in operation / under construction / proposed). Utilisation: 1,053.95 of 1,410.25 MLD assessed (74.7%); Telangana only 16.0 of 115.75 MLD (13.8%) vs Maharashtra 1,007.95 of 1,264.5 MLD (79.7%).

water_quality.note: Series years are not like-for-like: 70 stations carry CPCB Polluted River Stretches 2022 maxima (2019-21, stored as 2021 values); 19 are NWMP-only or AP-MPR-only; Telangana stations have Jun-Jul 2021 monthly samples (the only two comparable points, hence the only real trends); AP stations are single Jan 2025 values. No station has a continuous annual series. Worst station: Vasistha D/s Narasapuram, BOD 58.0 mg/l (2019-21 max). Worst stretch: Maharashtra Godavari main stem, BOD max 28.0 mg/l (Kapila-Godavari confluence), Priority II. Worst DO: Nakkavagu at Bachugudem, 1.6 mg/l (Jun 2021).

people.note: The summed town population is NOT the corridor population; see population below.

industries.note: 10 rows: 2 with a consented capacity figure (Waluj CETP, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, 10 MLD; Andhra Paper Ltd, Rajahmundry, 31.53 MLD; total 41.53 MLD) and 8 aggregate/belt rows with no figure. Effluent figures are consented capacities, never measurements, and are not added to any drain load. No CETP at all in the Andhra Pradesh Godavari stretch; no Godavari equivalent of the Yamuna GPI inspection exists.

drain_courses.note: No drain course geometry is published for any Godavari drain; no OSM way carries a named Godavari drain course.
